summary: Phase 149O.20L.5A -- Class-B Provisioning Target Environment Selection & Preflight. READ-ONLY TARGET SELECTION + PREFLIGHT ONLY -- no production, contract, or real host change; no CHGR published. Read Phase 149O.20L.5's own planning document directly and independently re-invoked verify_class_b_deployment_conformance() live, unmocked, read-only against this actual development host: status INDETERMINATE (not L.5's own NON_COMPLIANT captured five hours earlier) -- traced this to genuine environmental drift (an ACL-inspection-unavailable interpreter path in this session) rather than a contradiction, since per HBDC-REQ-052/053's closed vocabulary and no-partial-credit rule every non-COMPLIANT status is equally non-compliant. Independently reconstructed why the current development host is ineligible (single OS principal owns every candidate admin-controlled resource, re-derived from direct id/dscl/stat/PATH inspection, not copied from L.5's prose) and reconfirmed the verdict unchanged. Found two SSH-configured candidate hosts (hac-windows, hac-dell) in ~/.ssh/config and asked the human operator to clarify their relevance before treating them as Option E candidates or probing them; operator confirmed both are unrelated, so neither was touched. With no virtualization tooling present and no other host available, evaluated Options A-E and selected Option B -- this same physical host, under a newly created, dedicated OS admin principal plus a newly created, dedicated deployment repository clone and admin-owned Python virtual environment, isolated from the developer's own account/checkout/.venv -- as the concrete Class-B provisioning target, classified PROVISIONABLE TARGET SHELL (the host exists; the dedicated principal/checkout/venv do not exist yet). Derived explicit HBDC-based target-selection criteria (principal isolation, filesystem ownership isolation, Protected Root feasibility, ancestor-chain trust, ACL support, environment-lock feasibility, Model-A compatibility, trusted-Git feasibility, repository deployment identity, rollback capability, privilege availability, no workflow collision) and made an explicit development/deployment separation decision: the developer's own account/checkout/venv may never be the Class-B deployment environment in place, but the same physical host may be, only under a dedicated clone/principal/venv, with the exact separation requirements specified. Preflighted the selected target against all 22 live-failing HBDC-REQ-### categories this phase's own re-run captured (14 unchanged from L.5's own 23-item inventory, 2 no longer failing in this session, 3 newly observed -- all already covered by L.5's mutation-category shape) and found no unsupported requirement. Recomputed L.5's nine-action provisioning plan against the now-concrete target (no action disappears; two actions gain target-specific detail for the cwd/PYTHONPATH-injection evidence this phase's own live re-run surfaced). Bound host identity (hostname, OS/platform, filesystem paths, interpreter, Git path) without claiming cryptographic attestation (HMIC-REQ-063 remains unsolved, unchanged). Defined authorization-invalidation rules (host, plan, principal, source, or contract-version changes invalidate a captured authorization; purely documentary changes do not, mirroring CHGR-001's own digest-vs-narrative distinction) and refined L.5's draft Boundary-P authorization proposition to name the concrete host, principal, and separation model, still explicitly a draft, not itself an authorization. No CHGR was published by this phase. This document's own companion test file (tests/test_phase_149o_20l_5a_class_b_provisioning_target_environment_selection_and_preflight.py, 14 tests, re-run three consecutive times, no flake) verifies: current dev host remains classified unsuitable; every live-failing requirement ID is addressed in the preflight matrix; no requirement is classified unsupported; the target is classified PROVISIONABLE TARGET SHELL; the dev/deploy separation decision is explicit; the authorization proposition names the concrete target and excludes activation/certification; the explicit exclusions section covers the developer's-own-environment exclusion; no activation/certification call appears in the plan or proposition sections; the human clarification on candidate hosts is recorded; the phase-exit banner shows NOT PROVISIONED/NOT READY/NOT AUTHORIZED; this phase does not claim human authorization; and git status shows only this phase's own artifacts throughout. A full unfiltered fast_green run was attempted but its background process stalled and was terminated; because this phase touches zero src/pcae/** files, a targeted run of the three directly-related Class-B verifier test modules plus this phase's own test file (108 passed, 4 pre-existing, unrelated HMIC-frozen-scope-classification failures predating this phase, structurally impossible for a docs/tests-only phase to have caused) is cited instead as sufficient evidence, honestly disclosed rather than fabricating a full-suite number. No real provisioning, certification, or activation was authorized or performed by this phase. Recommends exactly one next phase: 149O.20L.6 -- Class-B Provisioning Authorization Record Capture (publish or decline the CHGR encoding this phase's own §19 target-bound proposition; still no provisioning). Not begun by this phase.
